title: Integral geometric fibres of a local regular morphism of strictly local schemes
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a local morphism between Noetherian strictly local schemes, where strictly local means the spectrum of a henselian local ring with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Assume that $f$ is regular: it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and its fibres remain regular after every finite extension of their residue fields [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For every geometric point $\bar z\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the geometric fibre $Y\times_X\bar z$ is nonempty and integral, that is, reduced and irreducible.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.3, printed pp.284–285. The nonemptiness follows from faithful flatness of a flat local ring map; integrality is the stated lemma.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ for the given strictly henselian local rings. Choose a prime $\ell$ different from the characteristic of the residue field of $A$, and set $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. The image of $\ell$ lies outside the maximal ideal of $A$, hence is a unit in $A$ and also in $B$. Fix a point $z\in X$, put $k=\kappa(z)$, and let $L/k$ be any finite field extension. Write $g:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ and $W_L=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$, with projections $p:W_L\to Y$ and $q:W_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. The map $g$ is affine: the inverse image of any affine open of $X$ is either empty or $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Thus it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $W_L=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A L)$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.3, printed pp.284–285, using Proposition 4.2.1, printed p.281.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-regular-etale-direct-image-base-change] to $f$, $g$ and the constant module sheaf $\Lambda_{\operatorname{Spec}L}$ in degree zero. All its hypotheses hold: $X,Y$ are Noetherian, $f$ is regular, $\ell$ is invertible, and $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by Step 1. It gives $f^*Rg_*\Lambda\simeq Rp_*q^*\Lambda$. The exactness and constant-ring comparison in [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identify $q^*\Lambda$ with $\Lambda_{W_L}$ and commute $f^*$ with degree-zero cohomology. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](2), applied to the left exact direct-image functors with enough injectives specified in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], degree-zero cohomology of $Rg_*\Lambda$ is $g_*\Lambda$, and similarly for $p$. Forgetting module coefficients commutes with these inverse and derived direct images by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients](1),(2). We obtain an isomorphism of abelian sheaves $f^{-1}g_*\Lambda\simeq p_*\Lambda_{W_L}$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.3, printed pp.284–285, using Proposition 4.2.1, printed p.281.

proof.text: Choose a geometric point $\bar y$ over the closed point of $Y$ and put $\bar x=f\bar y$. Since $f$ is local, $\bar x$ lies over the closed point of $X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] on both $X$ and $Y$, and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] to $f$ and $g_*\Lambda$. Together with the isomorphism of Step 2 this gives $\Gamma(Y,p_*\Lambda_{W_L})\simeq(p_*\Lambda_{W_L})_{\bar y}\simeq(f^{-1}g_*\Lambda)_{\bar y}\simeq(g_*\Lambda)_{\bar x}\simeq\Gamma(X,g_*\Lambda)$. The evaluation formula in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] identifies the outer groups with $\Gamma(W_L,\Lambda)$ and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}L,\Lambda)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], the latter group is $\Lambda$: the spectrum of a field is one point. Consequently $\Gamma(W_L,\Lambda)$ has exactly $\ell$ elements.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.3, printed pp.284–285, using Proposition 4.2.1, printed p.281.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], these sections are precisely the Zariski-locally constant maps $|W_L|\to\mathbf F_\ell$. If $W_L$ were empty there would be only one such map, contradicting $\ell>1$. If $W_L=U\amalg V$ with $U,V$ nonempty open-and-closed subsets, the $\ell^2$ maps taking independently chosen constant values on $U$ and $V$ would be distinct sections, contradicting the cardinality $\ell$. Therefore $W_L$ is nonempty and connected.

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps, followed by the elementary finite-cardinality connectedness argument.

proof.text: The regularity hypothesis on $f$, interpreted using [def-pc-scheme-fibre], says exactly that $W_L=(Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k)\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a regular scheme for every finite $L/k$. Here regular includes locally Noetherian, as in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Step 4 supplies nonemptiness and connectedness, so [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes $W_L$ integral. In the affine presentation of Step 1, [def-pc-integral-scheme] therefore says that $B\otimes_A L$ is an integral domain.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.3.2.3, printed pp.284–285, using Proposition 4.2.1, printed p.281.

proof.text: Put $S=B\otimes_A k$. The balanced tensor relations identify $S\otimes_k L$ with $B\otimes_A L$: the map sends $(b\otimes c)\otimes a$ to $b\otimes ca$, and its inverse sends $b\otimes a$ to $(b\otimes1)\otimes a$. Step 5 proves that these rings are domains for every finite $L/k$. Apply [lem-per-geometric-integrality-finite-field-test] to the commutative $k$-algebra $S$. For the field $\Omega$ of any given geometric point $\bar z\to X$ over $z$, it follows that $S\otimes_k\Omega\cong B\otimes_A\Omega$ is a domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its spectrum is exactly $Y\times_X\bar z$; by [def-pc-integral-scheme] this spectrum is nonempty and integral, as required. This last passage uses no Noetherian assumption on $\Omega$-base-changed fibres.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q40-ff07c745a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and the new node in full, all 15 cited statements, ILO XVII 4.2.1 (p.281) and 4.3.2.3 (pp.284-285), and Stacks 0FWF together with the definition of geometrically integral. The statement is unchanged and matches ILO 4.3.2.3. Step 1: the prime is chosen away from the residue characteristic, so it is a unit in A and B; Spec L -> X is affine, hence qcqs; W_L = Spec(B⊗_A L). Step 2: the regular base-change node (ILO 4.2.1, here with n=1) has every hypothesis met; degree-zero cohomology is taken through the exact inverse image, H0 Rg_* = g_*, and forgetting coefficients. Step 3: X and Y are both strictly henselian and f is local, so global sections equal stalks at the closed geometric points, and the stalk of the inverse image matches the stalk downstairs; this gives #Γ(W_L,F_ℓ) = ℓ. Step 4 is genuinely elementary: an empty W_L gives 1 section and a nontrivial clopen splitting gives at least ℓ^2. Step 5: W_L is regular (and locally Noetherian), nonempty and connected, so lem-sc-regular-connected-integral makes it integral. Step 6: 0FWF passes from all finite L to any geometric field Ω, writing out S⊗_k L ≅ B⊗_A L; this avoids assuming the Ω-fibre is Noetherian. The new node is exactly Stacks 0FWF (2)⇒(1), which needs no finiteness hypothesis. I tested it on k, k[ε]/(ε²), the zero ring and a separable field extension. It is self-contained, its blueprint fields are correct, and it duplicates nothing: 0FWF appears only in this delivery, and the geometric-reducedness and geometric-integrality nodes in trf/sbc do not state the criterion. There is no cycle (closure checked against the item and both citers), no SGA source, and every step is under 2000 characters (at most 1021). The three declared tool uses (constant-sheaf sections, constant-module inverse image, forgetting coefficients) are accepted; the other off-unit citations are slopmaster2-closed, Mathlib leaves or definitions. No changes.
